ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Organism-dependent activity

A laboratory finds that linezolid inhibits growth of an enterococcal isolate without rapid killing, but kills a susceptible streptococcal isolate under the test conditions. Which conclusion best interprets these findings?

  1. Static or cidal behavior can depend on the organism and test conditions
  2. The laboratory must be wrong because each drug has one universal killing label
  3. Linezolid has become a beta-lactam against streptococci
  4. A cidal test result proves activity at every infection site
  5. A static test result proves the drug cannot ever be clinically useful
Answer and explanation

Static or cidal behavior can depend on the organism and test conditions

The drug class alone does not establish an identical killing pattern for every organism.

Option explanations

Static or cidal behavior can depend on the organism and test conditions: The drug class alone does not establish an identical killing pattern for every organism.

The laboratory must be wrong because each drug has one universal killing label: Antibacterial behavior is not universally fixed across organisms and conditions.

Linezolid has become a beta-lactam against streptococci: The target mechanism does not change drug class in this way.

A cidal test result proves activity at every infection site: Distribution, exposure and the clinical setting remain important.

A static test result proves the drug cannot ever be clinically useful: Clinical effectiveness is not excluded solely by the bacteriostatic label.
